chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.' What is your view if the two judges seek permission, so they both say to the man and the woman, 'Is it not that you have both made your matter to us regarding reconciliation and separation?' So the man and the woman say, 'Yes'. So they bear witness with that upon them both. Is their separation allowed? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but it does not happen except upon purity of the woman, from without copulation from the husband.'

It was said to him (peace be upon him), 'What is your view if one of the two judges says, 'I have separated them,' and the other says, 'I have not separated them'?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Separation does not happen until they both agree upon the separation. So when they are both gathered upon the separation, their separation is allowed.'

key_terms.حَكَمٌ: Arbitrator/Judge appointed to resolve marital disputes
key_terms.طُهْرٌ: Purity (state of being free from major/minor impurity, specifically without intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for marital arbitrators to legally separate a couple according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the procedural mechanics of Surah An-Nisa 4:35, emphasizing that the arbitrators' authority to separate the couple is contingent upon the spouses' explicit consent and the wife's state of ritual purity (taharah) without recent intercourse. It further establishes a critical jurisprudential principle that the legal act of separation (tafreeq) requires the consensus of both appointed judges, preventing unilateral decrees and ensuring judicial unity in resolving marital discord.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [4:35] then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family, ‘What is yourasws view if the two judges seek permission, so they both say to the man and the woman, ‘Is it not that you have both made your matter to us regarding the reconciliation, and the separation?’ So the man and the woman say, ‘Yes’. So witnessed bear witness with that upon them both. Is their separating them allowed?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, but it does not happen except upon purity from the woman, from without copulation from the husband’.

It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if one of the two judges has effected separation between the two, and the other one says, ‘I will not affect separation between them both’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Separation does not happen until they both agree upon the separation. So when they are both gathered upon the separation, their separation is allowed’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘. . . an arbitrator from his people and an arbitrator from her people’ who then by the permission of both parties and with their stipulation that their decision must be accepted as binding. They then agree in the presence of witnesses; if the decision of the arbitrators to separate them is permissible. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is permissible, however, it must take place in a Hayd (menses)-free period and without sexual intercourse by the husband.’
It then was asked, ‘What happens if one of the arbitrators decides to separate them and the other disagrees?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘It cannot take place unless they both agree for separation. If they both agreed then separation is permissible.’”
